source_text: εἰσηγήσατο, προθέμενος ἅμα μὲν τοῦτο τὸ κεφάλαιον, ὃ νυνὶ μέτειμεν, ἅμα δὲ καὶ τῶν μεγαλοδωρεῶν καὶ τῆς ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι ἀναγεννήσεως τὸ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν πατέρα ἐπίκοινον τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος· ἔτι δὲ καὶ ὅτι τὸ «ὁ θεὸς» ὄνομα ἕν τε καὶ ἴσως ἐστὶν τῇ τριάδι· καὶ ἰσοδυνάμως ἀεὶ ἐνεργεῖ ἐπικληθεὶς ὅ τε θεὸς πατὴρ ὅ τε θεὸς υἱὸς ὅ τε θεὸς πνεῦμα· Κορινθίοις γράφων δημηγορεῖ· «ἀλλὰ ἀπελούσασθε, ἀλλὰ ἐδικαιώθητε, ἀλλὰ ἡγιάσθητε ἐν τῷ ὀνό ματι τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν.» διὸ οἱ κοινωνοῦντες αὐτῷ ὅ ἐστιν οἱ ἀξιούμενοι ἁγιάζεσθαι ὑπ' αὐτοῦ καὶ δικαιοῦσθαι καὶ σοφίζεσθαι, εἴρηνται, ὡς ὁ αὐτὸ ἀπόστολος Ἑβραίους διδάσκει· «μέτοχοι πνεύματος ἁγίου.» καὶ Ἐφεσίοις δὲ γράφει· «ἐν ᾧ καὶ πιστεύσαντες ἐσφραγίσθητε τῷ πνεύματι τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῷ ἁγίῳ.» δῆλον γάρ, ὡς οἱ σφραγιζόμενοι, τουτέστιν ἁγιαζόμενοι, μετέχουσιν, ἀλλ' οὐ μετέχονται. καὶ γὰρ εἰ κτίσμα ἐτύγχανεν ὂν τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἢ ὁ υἱός, ποῦ ἦν χρεία τὸ κτίσμα ἁγιάζειν καὶ ποιεῖν τὴν πλήρωσιν, καίτοι τοῦ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἀποχρώντως ἡγιακότος; οἱ γοῦν κτιστοὶ ἀκτίστου τὸ χρῖσμα τοῦτο εἰδότες, οὐκ οἴκοθεν παρέχομεν τὸν ἁγιασμόν, ἀλλὰ φαμέν· ὁ θεὸς ἁγιάσαι σε. καὶ πρὸς ἕτερον δὲ ὁμόλογον καὶ κραταιὸν βαδιοῦμαι δικαίωμα, μεθ' ὃ οὐδὲ τοῖς μεμελετηκόσιν ἀναισχυντεῖν ἐξέσται τοῦτο ποιεῖν. ὁ τοῦ παντὸς δεσπότης, περὶ μὲν τοῦ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ ἑαυτοῦ ἀπολελυμένως διαταξάμενος· «βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ,» οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἐπήγαγεν· «καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος,» ἀλλὰ προσέθηκεν· «τοῦ ἁγίου». ὥστε μονονουχὶ ὑποβεβηκότως αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐμνήσθη, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀναβεβηκότως διὰ τὸ ἐκεῖνο εἶναι τῇ φύσει, ὅ εἰσιν αἱ αὐτοτελεῖς ὑποστάσεις, ἃς ἐσήμανεν τὸ ἓν ὄνομα, ᾧ καὶ αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα συμπροσηγορεύθη· καὶ παραλλήλως διὰ τὸ ἐκεῖνο καθεστάναι τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, ὅ ἐστιν τῇ θεότητι ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ· οἷς συνεμνημονεύθη, ὡς τὸ δὴ λεγόμενόν ἐστι πρόδηλον καὶ τυφλῷ. ἀλλὰ τοῦτο μὲν πλείονος ἔχεται θεολογίας· ἵνα δὲ ῥᾳδίως πιστεύηται θεότητος μόνης ἴδιον ὑπάρχειν τὸ καλεῖσθαι, καὶ εἶναι φύσει ἅγιόν τε δίκαιόν τε, ἔτι μὴν τὸ ἁγιάζειν καὶ δικαιοῦν τὰ οἰκεῖα κτίσματα, ὅμοια ὑμνημένα εἰσὶν περὶ μὲν τοῦ πατρὸς, ὡς ἡνίκα αὐτὸς ὁ υἱὸς παρὰ Ἰωάννῃ λέγῃ· «πάτερ ἅγιε, τήρησον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου,» καὶ πάλιν· «ἁγίασον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ σου· ὁ λόγος ὁ σὸς ἀλήθειά ἐστιν,» καὶ αὖθις· «πάτερ δίκαιε.» καὶ ὡς ὅταν προφητεύωσιν, Ἰεζεκιὴλ μέν· «καὶ γνώτωσαν, ὅτι ἐγὼ κύριος ὁ ἁγιάζων αὐτούς,» ∆αυὶδ δὲ ἐν ιʹ ψαλμῷ· «δίκαιος κύριος, καὶ δικαιοσύνην ἠγάπησεν· εὐθύτητας ἴδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ,» καὶ ἕτερος· «καὶ πάντες οἱ ἡγιασμένοι ὑπὸ τὰς χεῖράς σου, καὶ ὑπὸ σέ εἰσιν.» καὶ ὡς ὅταν Παῦλος ἐπιστέλλῃ πρὸς μὲν Θεσσαλονικέας· «αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ἁγιάσαι ὑμᾶς ὁλοτελεῖς,» πρὸς δὲ Ῥωμαίους· «θεὸς ὁ δικαιῶν· τίς ὁ κατακρίνων;» πρὸς δὲ Ἑβραίους· «ἵνα ᾖ ἡ παρθένος ἁγία σώματι καὶ πνεύματι,» ὡς ἐγχωροῦντος τοῦ, ἢ κατ' οἰκείαν τροπὴν μὴ εἶναι αὐτὴν ἁγίαν, ἢ κατ' ἀρετὴν ἁγιάζεσθαι. λέγει δ' ἐνταῦθα, τὴν μὲν ἕξιν «πνεῦμα», τὴν δὲ πρακτικὴν ἐνέργειαν «σῶμα», κατὰ Ἡσαίαν προφητεύοντα· «καὶ γνώσονται οἱ τῷ πνεύματι πλανώμενοι σύνεσιν·» ὅ ἐστιν, οἱ τῇ πράξει ἢ τῇ ἕξει πλανώμενοι. περὶ δὲ τοῦ υἱοῦ, ὡς ἡνίκα εὐφημῆται· «εἷς ἅγιος, εἷς κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός,» καὶ ὡς αἱ Πράξεις διαλέγονται· «ἀπέκτειναν τοὺς προκαταγγείλαντας περὶ 60 τῆς ἐλεύσεως τοῦ δικαίου» καὶ καθὰ Πέτρος ἔφη· «Χριστὸς ἅπερ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἀπέθανεν, δίκαιος ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων.» καὶ ἐκ τῶν τοιούτων τοίνυν λογίων δέον, εἰ τὰ δίκαια πράττειν ἐβούλοντο, ποδηγεῖσθαι ἐπὶ τὸν θεὸν ἀνυμνεῖν τὸ πνεῦμα· τοῦτο μὲν οὐ ποιοῦσιν, φάσκουσιν δέ, ὅτι οἱ ἄγγελοι οὐχ ἡγιάσθησαν, καὶ ὅμως ἅγιοί εἰσιν·
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: Therefore Paul, who was able both to speak and to set out patterns of faith,] introduced it, setting forth at once both this heading which we are now pursuing, and at the same time the sharing of the Holy Spirit with God the Father in the great gifts and in the rebirth in baptism; and further also that the name 'God' is one and belongs equally to the Trinity; and that, when called upon, God the Father and God the Son and God the Spirit always work with equal power. Writing to the Corinthians he declares publicly: 'But you were washed, but you were justified, but you were sanctified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.' Therefore those who share in him, that is, those counted worthy to be sanctified and justified and made wise by him, have been called, as the same apostle teaches the Hebrews, 'partakers of the Holy Spirit.' And to the Ephesians he writes: 'In whom also, having believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of the promise.' For it is clear that those who are sealed, that is, sanctified, share in him, but are not shared in. For indeed, if the Holy Spirit or the Son happened to be a creature, where was the need for the creature to sanctify and to make up the fullness, although God the Father had sanctified sufficiently? We created beings at any rate, knowing this anointing to be of the uncreated one, do not supply the sanctification from our own house, but we say: 'May God sanctify you.' And I will go on also to another acknowledged and strong plea, after which not even those who have practised being shameless will be able to do this. The Master of the universe, having given command concerning God the Father and himself without qualification, 'baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son,' did not simply go on, 'and of the Spirit,' but added, 'the Holy.' So that he not only did not mention him in a lower way, but even in a higher way, because he is by nature that which the self-complete hypostases are, which the one name signified, with which the Spirit himself also was named together; and in parallel, because the Holy Spirit is established as that which the Father and his Son are in Godhead, with whom he was mentioned together, as is, as the saying goes, plain even to a blind man. But this belongs to a fuller theology. But so that it may be readily believed that it is proper to Godhead alone to be called, and to be by nature, both holy and righteous, and further to sanctify and justify its own creatures, like things have been sung concerning the Father, as when the Son himself in John says: 'Holy Father, keep them in your name,' and again: 'Sanctify them in your truth; your word is truth,' and once more: 'Righteous Father.' And as when they prophesy, Ezekiel: 'And let them know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them,' and David in the tenth Psalm: 'The Lord is righteous, and he loved righteousness; his eyes saw uprightness,' and another: 'And all those sanctified are under your hands, and they are under you.' And as when Paul writes to the Thessalonians: 'And may the God of peace himself sanctify you wholly,' and to the Romans: 'It is God who justifies; who is the one who condemns?' and to the Hebrews: 'that the virgin may be holy in body and spirit,' as it being possible either that by her own turning she is not holy, or that by virtue she is sanctified. And he here calls the settled state 'spirit' and the practical activity 'body', as Isaiah prophesies: 'And those who go astray in spirit will know understanding'; that is, those who go astray in deed or in settled state. And concerning the Son, as when he is praised: 'One is holy, one is Lord, Jesus Christ,' and as the Acts say: 'They killed those who announced beforehand about [printed line number 60, page debris] the coming of the Righteous One,' and as Peter said: 'Christ died for sinners, righteous on behalf of the unrighteous.' So from such oracles too they ought, if they wished to do what is just, to be guided on to hymning the Spirit as God. This they do not do, but they assert that the angels were not sanctified, and yet are holy, [the sentence continues in the next section].
pass_b_english: …set it out. In one stroke he put forward the very heading we are now pursuing, and with it the Holy Spirit’s fellowship with God the Father in the great gifts and in the rebirth of baptism. He showed too that the name “God” is one and belongs equally to the Trinity, and that God the Father, God the Son and God the Spirit, when called upon, always work with equal power. Writing to the Corinthians, he declares: “But you were washed, but you were justified, but you were sanctified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God” (1 Corinthians 6:11).

That is why those who share in him, that is, those counted worthy to be sanctified, justified and made wise by him, are called “partakers of the Holy Spirit” (Hebrews 6:4), as the same apostle teaches the Hebrews. And to the Ephesians he writes: “In him you also, when you believed, were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise” (Ephesians 1:13). It is plain that those who are sealed, that is, sanctified, share in him; they are not shared in. Indeed, if the Holy Spirit or the Son were a creature, what need would there be for a creature to sanctify and to fill up what is lacking, when God the Father had already sanctified enough? We who are created know that this anointing belongs to the uncreated one. So we do not supply sanctification from our own store, but we say, “May God sanctify you.”

I will go on to another proof, agreed by all and strong, after which not even those who have trained themselves in shamelessness will be able to keep it up. The Master of the universe, after giving his command about God the Father and himself without any qualifier, “baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son” (Matthew 28:19), did not simply go on, “and of the Spirit,” but added, “the Holy.” So he did not merely avoid naming him in a lower way; he named him in a higher one. For the Spirit is by nature what the self-complete hypostases are, which the one name signified, the name under which the Spirit himself was named with them. And in the same way the Holy Spirit is established as what the Father and his Son are in Godhead, and he was named together with them. That much, as the saying goes, is plain even to a blind man.

But this belongs to a fuller theology. Still, so that it may be readily believed that it is proper to the Godhead alone to be called holy and righteous, and to be so by nature, and further to sanctify and justify its own creatures, Scripture sings of the Father in the same terms. So the Son himself says in John, “Holy Father, keep them in your name” (John 17:11), and again, “Sanctify them in your truth; your word is truth” (John 17:17), and once more, “Righteous Father” (John 17:25). So too the prophets: Ezekiel, “And let them know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them” (Ezekiel 20:12); David in the eleventh Psalm, “The Lord is righteous, and he has loved righteousness; his eyes have seen uprightness” (Psalm 11:7); and another, “And all who are sanctified are under your hands, and they are under you” (Deuteronomy 33:3). So too Paul, writing to the Thessalonians, “May the God of peace himself sanctify you completely” (1 Thessalonians 5:23); to the Romans, “It is God who justifies; who is the one who condemns?” (Romans 8:33-34); and to the Hebrews, “that the virgin may be holy in body and spirit” (1 Corinthians 7:34). He speaks as one for whom it is possible either that she, by turning of her own will, is not holy, or that she is made holy by virtue. By “spirit” he here means the settled state of the soul, and by “body” its practical activity, as Isaiah prophesies: “And those who go astray in spirit will come to understanding” (Isaiah 29:24), that is, those who go astray in deed or in settled state.

And of the Son, as when he is praised, “One is holy, one is Lord, Jesus Christ”; and as the Acts say, “They killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One” (Acts 7:52); and as Peter said, “Christ died for sinners, the righteous for the unrighteous” (1 Peter 3:18). From such oracles, then, they ought, if they wished to act justly, to be led on to praising the Spirit as God. This they do not do. Instead they assert that the angels were not sanctified and yet are holy…

choices.issue: Garbled machine draft, misread words, broken sentence, abbreviated references
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u15): retranslated from the Greek. The old English read ἴσως as 'perhaps' ('the name God is one and perhaps belongs to the Trinity'), turned καίτοι τοῦ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἀποχρώντως ἡγιακότος into 'acting without debt to God the Father', made 'we created beings ... of the uncreated' into 'the creatures ... from the Creator', read ἕξιν as 'the sixth [thing]', called the Spirit's elevation in Matthew 28:19 'mentioned once', broke off at 'who is in divinity the Pa—' and restarted with 'Even the Son [is so described]', gave 'Father, judge' for 'Righteous Father', and printed the line number '[about 60]'. References: (1 Cor 6:11), (Eph 1:13), (Matt 28:19), (1 Thess 5:23) written out in full; (Romans 8:33) -> (Romans 8:33-34); Deuteronomy 33:3 and Acts 7:52 added; Greek Psalm 10 given as the eleventh; brackets [noted], [is so described], [thing] removed.

choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence; the subject, Paul, is the last word of the previous section. Only the words this section holds are translated, so the English opens with an ellipsis.

choices.term: τὸ «ὁ θεὸς» ὄνομα ἕν τε καὶ ἴσως ἐστὶν τῇ τριάδι
choices.english: the name “God” is one and belongs equally to the Trinity
choices.why: ἴσως pairs with ἰσοδυνάμως in the next clause; the argument is equality, not doubt.

choices.english: to fill up what is lacking
choices.why: If the Father sanctified sufficiently, a creature would have nothing left to complete.

choices.english: we do not supply sanctification from our own store
choices.why: οἴκοθεν, 'from home', means from one's own resources; Didymus speaks as one of the created (first person plural).

choices.english: those who have trained themselves in shamelessness will be able to keep it up
choices.why: τοῦτο ποιεῖν takes up ἀναισχυντεῖν: after this proof, not even practised shamelessness can go on denying.

choices.english: he did not merely avoid naming him in a lower way; he named him in a higher one
choices.why: Adding 'Holy' raised the Spirit's mention rather than lowering it. Didymus uses μονονουχί with οὐ ... ἀλλὰ καί for 'not only not ... but also' (as in 6.10, μονονουχὶ δοῦλον οὐ γέγραπται, ἀλλὰ καί).

choices.english: plain even to a blind man
choices.why: A proverb, and Didymus was himself blind; kept literally.

choices.english: settled state of the soul / practical activity
choices.why: ἕξις is the inner disposition, set against outward deeds; 'of the soul' is added in English to make the contrast with 'body' clear and adds no claim.
Didymus names Hebrews, but the words are 1 Corinthians 7:34. His attribution is kept in the text and the verse actually quoted is cited; recorded in problems.
Greek Psalm 10 is English Psalm 11; the verse quoted is Psalm 11:7.
The words are LXX Deuteronomy 33:3 (Moses' blessing): 'all the sanctified are under your hands'; KJV 'all his saints are in thy hand' is the same verse.
60 is a printed line number inside the Greek, page debris; skipped.
ἅπερ makes no sense here; read as ὑπὲρ ('for'), the reading the following ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων supports. The New Testament text has ἅπαξ περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ('once for sins'). Recorded in problems.

choices.term: ποδηγεῖσθαι ἐπὶ τὸν θεὸν ἀνυμνεῖν τὸ πνεῦμα
choices.english: to be led on to praising the Spirit as God
choices.why: Read as ἐπὶ τὸ θεὸν ἀνυμνεῖν; the literal 'to be guided to God, to hymn the Spirit' gives the same claim less clearly. Recorded in problems.
The sentence runs on into the next section (οὐ προσέχοντες, 'not noticing'); the English ends with an ellipsis.
